html:
The Saya San rebellion was a peasant uprising that began in Tharrawaddy in December 1930 and spread across Lower Burma. Its leader, Saya San, a former monk and healer, proclaimed himself king.

Farmers were crushed by low rice prices, debt and the head tax. Rebels armed with swords and protective tattoos fought British troops and police.

The revolt was put down by 1932, and Saya San was hanged. Some thousands of rebels died. The young lawyer Ba Maw defended him in court, and the revolt inspired the students who formed the Thakin movement, including Aung San. See British Burma.
